speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my assessment, how long has this symptom been present?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: ESR_and_CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work results are normal, which helps rule out active systemic infection or severe inflammatory arthritis like gout. Since the swelling and pain are progressive, has this been accompanied by any fever, chills, or a visible red streak extending from the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That specific mechanism of injury—where the finger is caught and pulled forcefully—is highly suspicious for a gamekeeper's thumb or a boutonnière deformity involving the ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) of the MCP joint. Did you feel or hear a distinct "pop" at the moment of injury, and when you make a fist, does your ring finger knuckle bend while the tip remains straight or deviates?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hand_XRay_Special_views
REQUEST TEST: UCL_Stress_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury, combined with a "pop" and the inability to fully bend the fingertip while the middle joint hyperextends, strongly suggests an ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) tear or a gamekeeper's thumb. The X-rays I requested were to rule out fractures; if they show no bone injury, we will proceed with the physical stress test to confirm the ligamentous instability. Have you noticed any significant weakness or inability to make a full fist with that hand?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint while the middle joint hyperextends, combined with the specific "pulling" injury mechanism, strongly points to an injury of the central slip of the extensor tendon. Can you confirm if you are unable to straighten your middle finger knuckle when you try to make a fist, and does pressing on the center of the dorsal aspect of the middle joint reproduce the pain?

REQUEST TEST: Central_Slip_Tendon_Integrity_Assessment
REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Hand_Flexor_Extensor_View

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The patient is unable to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right ring finger while attempting to make a fist, indicating a loss of active flexion at that specific joint. Pressing on the center of the dorsal aspect of the middle joint (proximal interphalangeal or PIP joint) reproduces significant pain and tenderness. The middle joint (PIP) appears to extend normally without hyperextension in the current assessment, but the inability to flex the DIP joint while the finger rests in extension is consistent with a disruption of the central slip mechanism or extensor tendon injury at the PIP level, often referred to as a boutonnière deformity mechanism.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boutonnière deformity of the right ring finger (Central slip tendon rupture).

The clinical picture of a "pop" during trauma, inability to actively flex the DIP joint, and focal tenderness over the center of the PIP joint is pathognomonic for this injury. The normal X-rays and lack of hyperextension rule out a frank gamekeeper's thumb (UCL tear) or fracture.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
